text:
alex: Quick question for y'all — we keep running into client incompat bugs when teams switch between our gRPC and REST surfaces. Do we standardize on a gateway that does protocol translation, or make clients do protocol negotiation + fallback? Need capture for quotas/telemetry/rollout UX.

kim: Gateway wins for DX imo. Clients stay thin. Gateway can centralize quotas, headers, and signal for console. downside: adds hops/latency and more surface area to instrument.

jordan: Agree on DX but worried about streaming fallbacks. If we transcode streaming -> long polling JSON we lose backpressure + cost profiles. Also protobuf -> json changes shape (enum names, oneofs).

maria: Hybrid idea: clients advertise preferred transport via a header and gateway routes to native backend when available, otherwise transcode. Example header:

```
Accept-Transport: application/grpc, application/json
X-Client-Version: 2.4.0
```

Gateway can set X-Observed-Transport when it forces a fallback.

alex: Nice. How do we keep quota attribution consistent? If gateway calls upstream as service account, telemetry shows gateway as caller and breaks tenant billing.

kim: Propagate tenant headers and cryptographically sign them so upstreams can verify provenance. e.g., X-Tenant-Id + X-Tenant-Sig = HMAC(tenant_id|ts).

jordan: Or pass through tokens and let upstreams do auth; but that means exposing more secrets to gateway unless gateway acts purely as proxy (no token swap). Tradeoff.

maria: For visibility we must attach transport metadata to traces/spans. Sample pseudo-instrumentation:

```
span.set_attribute("redwood.transport.requested", "grpc")
span.set_attribute("redwood.transport.actual", "json-transcoded")
```

That way console can filter by mismatches and show fallback counts.

deploy-bot: canary created: protocol-fallback-playbook v1 -> route rules: 1% -> gateway-transcode, 99% -> native routing. CI link: https://ci/redwood/1234 :rocket:

alex: Rollout signals we care about: p50/p95 latency, error rate, mismatch count (requested!=actual), per-tenant cost delta. Also need a UX in console to show which clients are on which path.

kim: Telemetry note — ensure gateway emits both request and upstream span so we can attribute token/usage correctly. Also sample logs should include: `tenant=acme path=/generate transport=transcoded latency_ms=142` for quick Kibana queries.

jordan: Can we avoid full transcode for streaming by offering a websocket bridge for browser clients? Less ideal but better perf than chunked polling.

maria: Good idea. Add websocket-adapter as a lightweight edge mode. Fallback order: native grpc -> websocket bridge -> json transcode.

alex: Ok — next steps: kim to draft gateway compatibility checklist (headers, sigs, telemetryAttrs), jordan to prototype websocket bridge, maria to author console signals + evals for quality regressions, I'll draft canary playbook.

kim: Working on checklist, will post RFC by EOD tomorrow. @maria fyi pls add console mocks :eyes:

maria: Will do. starting with a dashboard tile: percent_fallback_by_client and tenant_cost_delta.

alex: Quick poll — prefer gateway-first approach? react with :+1: for gateway, :heart: for client-negotiation.

kim: :+1:

jordan: :+1:

maria: :+1:

alex: Great, consensus. I'll write the playbook and link to the canary deploy. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
